title: PatientAgentBench — Whissle
label: Whissle
preliminary_reason: N = 6 is below the 30-unit threshold for a settled number

headline.label: Weighted aggregate (1–5)
headline.note: weighted mean of six rubric dimensions; weights below

what_measured: Whether a patient-facing health assistant handles a real patient's request end to end: does it complete the task, stay clinically safe, follow the correct workflow, triage at the right urgency, actually help, and hold a conversation a patient would tolerate. Six rubric dimensions, 1–5, weighted so safety counts most.
why_measured: Task-success alone rewards an assistant that books an appointment for someone describing a stroke. A weighted rubric is the only way to score the safety trade-off explicitly rather than average it away.
methodology: the deployed Whissle agent brain, unmodified
`harness_tools` — the benchmark's own ReAct harness, system prompt and 15 sandbox tools, with only the model swapped
the benchmark's system prompt is passed through verbatim; the deployed agent's own persona is not applied, which is what makes the number comparable to a published baseline
the benchmark's 15 sandbox tools, executed by the harness (not by the agent's own tool runtime)
per-dimension mean of 1–5 rubric scores; aggregate is the weight-normalised mean of the six dimension means
scoring_rule: aggregate = Σ(weight_d × mean_d) / Σ(weight_d) over the six rubric dimensions; pass = score ≥ 3

tables.title: Per-dimension detail
tables.note: Pass = score ≥ 3, scale 1–5. Weights sum to 8.3.

sampling.note: Strata are matched to the population within one case per cell; the table below is the audit of that match, not an assertion that it is exact.

baselines.comparability_note: No published PatientAgentBench baseline is registered in this harness, so no comparison table is shown. The paper's own leaderboard exists, but it was produced with K = 2 jury grading on an independent grader; quoting a K = 1 self-graded number against it would be a comparison of two different measurements, and we will not print one until the run is re-graded independently. Absence of a comparison here is a deliberate result, not a gap in the tooling.
baselines.published_protocol: K = 2 LLM jury, independent grader, full case set

limitations.text: The graders and simulators ran on the same vendor's model API as the agent under test. Held constant across runs this is a sound regression instrument; quoted against someone else's leaderboard it is not, because nothing rules out shared priors between the thing being measured and the ruler.

K = None — a single grading pass per rubric. The published protocol uses K = 2 and reports inter-rater agreement; at K = 1 the per-case `score_std` is structurally zero and the confidence intervals below reflect only between-case variance, not grader disagreement.
6 of 20 cases were drawn. The stratified draw controls task type and severity mix; it does not control for anything unobserved.
Rubric scores are bounded at 5, so a strong run compresses against the ceiling and the aggregate loses resolution exactly where improvements matter least.
This run is text. The deployed product is voice-first; ASR and TTS error are absent here by construction and a voice number will be lower for reasons that have nothing to do with clinical reasoning.

notes: The seeded stratified draw reproduces exactly for a given seed and population; the sampled case ids are listed in `summary.json` under `sampling.case_ids`.
Scores will not reproduce bit-for-bit: both the agent and the jury are sampled generative models.
